evidence.text:
The characters 史 (history), 吏 (government official), 使 (cause; use; instruct), and 事 (matter; work; affair) are all etymologically related and all derive from the same ancient character, depicting a hand (又) holding some object. 
There are various theories about theories about what this object is, including a writing utensil, a container for official documents, a flag, or a hunting tool.
These four characters were originally all written the same, but later marks were added to distinguish them.
職也。从史，之省聲。

Ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 又 (“hand”) + 中 (“a flagpole with a drum”) – flag in hand > to perform one's job. Compare 吏. Furthermore, both character are related to 史, which is a variant without the horizontal stroke on top.
Exopassive of 士 (OC *zrɯʔ, “to give or carry out an assignment; to serve”), literally “what has been assigned” (Schuessler, 2007).
Alternatively, based on Gong (2000), STEDT derives it from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *r-dzas (“thing”), whence Burmese စာ (ca, “thing”) and Tibetan རྫས (rdzas, “thing, object, matter”).
職也。从史，之省聲。
affair, matter, business; to serve; accident, incident

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: Oracle-bone and bronze component analysis; forms and senses for 事
evidence.text: The database reports that 甲骨文 forms for 事/史/吏/使 were initially one graph, analyzed as a hand holding an object, and later differentiated. It records 事 in bronze inscriptions for duties/official work, events, an office, and in one cited inscription for a verb meaning to send/command; it also gives later transmitted-text examples for matters, undertaking, and serving. The object held is disputed: scholarship cited there proposes a flag, a container for bamboo records, a writing brush, or a hunting implement. These are competing interpretations, not established identifications. Examples include 麥鼎 and 克鼎 for office/duty, 琱生簋 for event, and 小臣守簋 for command/serve.
evidence.kind: secondary scholarly database reporting primary inscription evidence
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — oracle-bone component analysis, 又

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: Graphic history and competing interpretations of 史 and related graphs
evidence.text: The database says 史、吏、事、使 were once a single graph, depicting a hand holding something, and became separate graphs. It attributes several rival identifications of the held object: a flag (吳其昌), a container for bamboo slips (王國維), a brush (馬敍倫), or a hunting tool (陳夢家); 徐中舒 proposed a forked hunting implement. It notes graphic differentiation in small-seal forms and cites a proposal that this differentiation occurred around Qin-Han. It also reports oracle-bone uses of 史 for an office/clan/person, matter, and ‘send’; bronze uses include office and uses interchangeable with 事 and 使. This does not establish the object's name or pronunciation, nor that 事 originated as a phonetic loan from a tool name.
evidence.kind: secondary scholarly database reporting primary inscription evidence and named scholarly analyses
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — oracle-bone component analysis, 史

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字古今文字資料庫 (Academia Sinica Character Database)
evidence.text: The database lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen form categories. Its summary says ancient 史、事、使 were the same graph depicting a hand holding an object; it reports hunting-tool and divination-tool interpretations for the held object. The page gives no date for an individual glyph instance, so it supports a sequence of script categories but not a precise first-attestation date.
evidence.title: 漢字「事」：字形演變

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字古今文字資料庫 (Academia Sinica Character Database)
evidence.field: Definitions and graphic-history notes for 事
evidence.text: The database lists senses including office/duty, occupation, matter, incident/change, serving, undertaking, administration, appointment, and use. Its note says ancient 事、使、史、吏 were originally one graph and later differentiated. The page is a dictionary summary; it does not establish a chronological order among all listed senses.
evidence.title: 漢字「事」：基本資料

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: Historical attestations and semantic uses of 事
evidence.text: The database cites bronze inscriptions for 事 meaning duty/office, event, and serving/commanding. It cites transmitted early texts for matters/events (including Analects 為政, ‘有事，弟子服其勞’) and for serving/undertaking (Analects 顏回, ‘請事斯語矣’; Xunzi 非相). Its examples distinguish evidence for word senses from the account of graphic development. The site gives inscription names and received-text citations but not exact archaeological dates or a complete textual dating argument; semantic chronology beyond the attested examples remains uncertain.
evidence.kind: secondary lexicographic database citing primary inscription and textual evidence
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 事

evidence.field: 說文 and phonological dictionary summary
evidence.text: The page reproduces the Shuowen gloss 職也 (‘office/duty’) and analysis 从史，之省聲, treating 史 as the semantic component and abbreviated 之 as phonetic. This is Xu Shen's historical analysis, not independent proof that the ancient graph was formed that way. The same page gives two Guangyun fanqie spellings, 側吏切 and 鉏吏切, reflecting distinct listed readings, and several reconstruction systems in its summary. Do not merge these with Baxter–Sagart readings.
evidence.kind: dictionary reference reporting Shuowen and rhyme-book data
evidence.title: 事 shì — 汉典

evidence.field: Oracle component account for 事; graphic history and bronze examples
evidence.text: The database describes oracle forms as hand (手) plus an unidentified component, depicting a hand holding something. It says the graphs 史、吏、事、使 later differentiated; in bronze forms an unbranched upper stroke is commonly assigned to 史 and a branched form to 吏/事. Bronze examples use 事 for duty, events, an office, and a command/serve verb. The identification of the held object is disputed: proposals include a flag, a document container, a brush, and hunting implements. These are source-reported analyses, not an established object identification.

evidence.field: Attested senses and cited texts for 事
evidence.text: The database reports bronze-inscription uses for duty/office (麥鼎, 克鼎), event (琱生簋), office (小盂鼎), and command or service (小臣守簋). It also cites received texts for events/matters, undertaking, appointment, and serving, and cites the Qin Shuihudi daybook manuscript for 百事凶. These examples establish several uses but do not by themselves date the earliest occurrence of each sense or prove a single linear semantic development.

evidence.field: 史 comparisons, inscriptions, and proposed graphic history
evidence.text: The database says 史、吏、事、使 began as one graph and lists competing identifications for the object held by the hand. It reports oracle-bone 史 usages for an office, clan/person, matter, and ‘send’; in bronze it reports office usages and cases interchangeable with 事 and 使. It presents Wang Guowei's account of later differentiation into distinct small-seal graphs as a proposal, not a settled date. This evidence does not establish that 史 was a phonetic component in 事.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The earliest individual attested 事 graph and its archaeological date were not established from inspected glyph images or a primary inscription catalogue; the databases list oracle-bone and bronze categories and selected examples without precise dates.

The held object's identity and name remain disputed. No independent evidence establishes the pronunciation of a depicted flag, writing implement, document container, divination tool, or hunting implement, so a whole-graph phonetic-loan account based on such an object is unsupported here.

The Shuowen explanation 从史，之省聲 is a later lexicographic analysis and conflicts with the paleographic account that 史、吏、事、使 differentiated from an earlier shared graph. Available sources do not settle whether any later component analysis should be called phonetic for the ancient graph.

No independently supported phonetic role for 史 in 事 was established; the similar modern readings cannot prove ancient sound function. No local reading row or external character page for 史 was successfully verified in this session.

Current kMandarin data for 事 was available only as a supplied local row; the official Unicode Unihan record endpoint was attempted and inaccessible. The same is true for 史; no host/component pronunciation comparison was therefore verified through official Unihan records.

No repeatable local extract is recommended: the inspected character-specific paleographic databases provide sufficient concise evidence for this entry, and reuse permissions for a broader extract were not verified.

The exact earliest attested instance and archaeological date of 事 were not established: the consulted databases label oracle-bone and bronze categories, but the accessible records do not date a first specimen.

The held object's original identity and name remain disputed. Since no independent evidence establishes the object's name or pronunciation, a whole-graph loan from that object's name is not demonstrated.

The Shuowen account 从史，之省聲 conflicts with the paleographic description of the related graphs as later differentiated from an earlier shared graph. The available sources do not establish a phonetic role for 史 in the ancient form of 事.

The local primary reading rows supplied in the task give Unihan kMandarin 事 shì and 史 shǐ, and Baxter–Sagart 2014 MC dzriH / OC *[m-s-]rəʔ-s for 事 and MC sriX / OC *s-rəʔ for 史. These are local structured data, not externally verified rows in this run. The official Unicode character pages failed to open, and no externally inspected primary Baxter–Sagart source was found. Current readings do not prove ancient phonetic function.

No source established a semantic chronology for all senses. The CUHK page supplies cited examples, including bronze inscriptions and the Shuihudi Qin manuscript, but not a complete dating argument for semantic extensions.

The relevant Academia Sinica character-specific page says All Rights Reserved, so it is not proposed as an image. The Xiaoxuetang query record and rights notice could not be inspected sufficiently to select an image. The Commons candidate ACC-s02204.svg had a description-page access failure; it is not selected.
No repeatable local text extract is recommended: reuse permission for a wider database extract was not verified and a concise character-specific citation suffices.
